questions.answer: I got 2/4 classes that I really wanted, so kind of okay.

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different compared to KU, since most classes was not tecahing "Hard law", but rather concepts. And it was kind of political.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More professors teaching, and the students was less invovled.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Internet Law
Family Property Law
Banking Law
Cybersecurity and the Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Internet Law and Banking Law, because they were most relevant compared to working with law, and most of the stuff taught could be used at home.

questions.answer: Mostly easy, it was very diversed. Didn't speak french though.

questions.answer: Most a more outgoing, more than danish people. So just talk to them.

questions.answer: Language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find the other danish exchange students and have fun.

questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and experince I gained throughout my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going from talking to friends and family at home most days to once or twice a month. And having a girlfriend at home.
